title: Which housing projects qualify for San Francisco’s union pension transfer-tax reduction?

beats.text: This is an investigative lead. Which housing projects can get San Francisco’s union pension tax reduction?

visual.sub: The transfer-tax reduction requires union construction and pension financing

beats.text: One condition is a $25 million pension investment still held when the property transfers.
Another is a share of rent-restricted homes. Ordinary private financing alone cannot qualify.
The investment trust supporting the law named three San Francisco housing developments.

visual.kicker: The investor that supported the law named three projects

beats.text: Its own schedule puts two of them below $25 million from this trust alone.
The third, Ventana, had $52 million in original financing from the trust.

visual.label: The investor that supported the law named three projects

beats.text: The City estimated up to $5 million a year in forgone tax. Its own analyst called that an overestimate.

visual.kicker: The advertised revenue figure was an upper estimate

beats.text: The model lacked data on which projects had qualifying pension owners.
Ventana later received approval for a separate grant of up to $10,000.
The records do not establish how much was collected.

visual.text: Office of Labor Standards Enforcement certificate

beats.text: A lead is a question, not an accusation.

chapters.p: The transfer-tax reduction requires union construction and pension financing
chapters.b: The investor that supported the law named three projects
chapters.o: The later Ventana transactions are different events
